title: Analytic separation of the regular representation of SL(2, R) into series
statement: Construct invariant projectors separating the discrete and continuous parts of \(L^2(SL(2,\mathbb R))\), and realize the two discrete parts as holomorphic Hardy boundary values on explicitly specified invariant domains. This is narrower than the Plancherel decomposition into all individual irreducibles.
status: As of 10 November 2026, resolved for this group. Spectral separation predates 1976; the specific invariant-domain and Hardy implementation was published by Gelfand and Gindikin in 1977, received 6 June 1977. The notebook projector formula needs the trace-factor correction recorded in its occurrence.

title: Arnold’s Möbius characterization of the Gelfand--Gindikin domains
statement: After Cayley conjugation, identify the two invariant open complex domains with strict Möbius contractions of the closed unit disc or its closed exterior into the corresponding open region in \(\mathbb{CP}^1\).
status: As of 10 November 2026, resolved by \citet[Proposition~9]{gelfandgindikin1977complex}. Published 1977 after the 6 September 1976 conjecture; the strictness and real-form conventions are essential.

title: Local point linearization of scalar second-order ODEs
statement: For a regular smooth scalar equation \(y''=F(x,y,y')\), determine whether a local nonsingular point transformation takes the equation to \(Y''=0\). The condition concerns the equation on an open set, not the quadratic coefficient along only one solution.
status: As of 10 November 2026, classically resolved by simultaneous vanishing of the Lie--Tresse invariants \(I,H\). Arnold explicitly presented nineteenth-century work; Cartan's 1924 connection theory and the 2008/2009 modern reconstruction verify the criterion. The notebook’s weaker one-solution implication is false.

title: Extension of four-dimensional supertranslations to the Poincaré superalgebra
statement: Adjoin Lorentz generators acting in the vector representation on translations and the Majorana spin representation on odd generators, with the odd bracket equivariant into translations. Construct the resulting \(N=1\) Lie superalgebra without central charges.
status: As of 10 November 2026, resolved before the 1976 question: the Gol'fand--Likhtman algebra circulated and was published in 1971. Likhtman's reproduced preprint carries a 12 April 1971 printing date. The semidirect-product construction verifies the mixed Jacobi identity through equivariance.

title: Stokes formula for closed superdomains with even boundary
statement: Construct the appropriate integral forms and boundary restriction for an oriented smooth \(p|q\) supermanifold with a specified embedded even boundary, and establish \(\int_{\mathcal D}d\omega=\int_{\partial\mathcal D}\iota^*\omega\) for compactly supported \((p-1)\)-degree integral forms; the notebook tests the boundary \(u_1^2+u_2^2+c\xi_1\xi_2-1=0\).
status: Solved by \citet[\S12]{bernsteinleites1977integral}, submitted 6 October 1976 and published in 1977. The submission predates the dated seminar; public circulation before that date has not been established. As of November 2026 this exact smooth-boundary statement is settled.

title: Reconstructing higher-rank commuting ordinary differential operators
statement: Recover a commuting algebra of scalar ordinary differential operators of generic spectral rank \(r>1\) from correctly normalized pointed-curve, spectral-bundle and local functional data, at least for smooth spectral curves and data in general position. A curve and an unframed bundle alone are not sufficient input.
status: As of November 2026, the generic smooth-curve inverse problem is solved by the abstract Drinfeld correspondence and Krichever's effective reconstruction. \citet[Theorem~2.3]{krichever1978commutative} corrects the earlier 1977 implementation; its received date is 15 February 1977. No claim of a complete classification of all singular or globally regular real cases is attached to this occurrence.

title: Boundary-compatible hypersimplicial chains for the first Pontryagin class
statement: Extend the double-zero and one-section-change loci to rational configuration-space chains assigned to hypersimplices, compatible with faces and satisfying \(\partial C(H)=C(\partial H)\), in the first-Pontryagin construction.
status: As of November 2026: solved before the 1977 exposition by the 1975 GGL construction. The notebook does not specify a separate stronger variant. Compare \citet[\S18 and \S\S27--28]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975calculus}.

title: Range and inversion of the line transform in three-space
statement: Characterize globally smooth rapidly decreasing line data that are integrals of a Schwartz function on \(\mathbb C^3\) or \(\mathbb R^3\), and reconstruct that function.
status: As of November 2026: solved before the talk by \citet[\S\S7--8, Theorems 1--2]{gelfand1967planes}. The notebook omits the global data class and real/complex cycle distinction.

title: Admissible algebraic complexes of lines
statement: For a closed irreducible algebraic three-dimensional line complex covering a dense open subset of \(\mathbb C^3\), determine when the differential inversion form descends from the scalar line data restricted to the complex, and classify such complexes near generic regular lines.
status: As of November 2026: the specified admissibility and generic classification were established in \citet[\S\S2--5]{gelfandgraev1968complexes}. The notebook's wording about already differentiated data is a partial match.

title: Poncelet closure for two conics
statement: For two nonsingular conics with smooth incidence elliptic curve, determine whether the consistent tangent iteration has a closed polygon, and characterize its period.
status: As of November 2026: classical; the translation point on the incidence elliptic curve is torsion precisely in the closing case. The exact source cited in the notes is \citet[\S I(d)]{griffiths1976abel}.

title: Counting Young-graph paths between prescribed endpoints
statement: Given \(\mu\subseteq\lambda\), count saturated Young-graph paths from \(\mu\) to \(\lambda\), equivalently compute the multiplicity of \(V^\mu\) in \(V^\lambda|_{S_{|\mu|}}\).
status: As of November 2026: the count is the skew-tableau number \(f^{\lambda/\mu}\), given exactly by the classical Jacobi--Trudi/Aitken determinant. The notebook states no further asymptotic or positivity demand. The checked later derivation is \citet[equation~(1.2)]{stanley2011skew}.

title: Ulam asymptotics and the Plancherel first row
statement: For a uniform permutation, or the ranks of an independent continuous sample, determine the leading asymptotic longest increasing-subsequence length.
status: As of November 2026: \(L_n/(2\sqrt n)\to1\) in probability. This is the 1977 first-order result of \citet[Corollaries~1--2]{vershikkerov1977asymptotics}; the separate fluctuation discussion is not folded into this solved question.

title: Description and Torelli information of rank-one representation packets
statement: For a fixed marked compact Riemann surface \(X\) and degree-zero line bundle \(L\), describe all characters with underlying holomorphic bundle \(L\), and determine the information about \(X\) retained by that embedded packet.
status: As of November 2026: the packet is a coset of the exponential of holomorphic periods; its embedded tangent space, integral marking, and intersection pairing recover the principally polarized Jacobian and hence the curve. These are the classical constructions and exercises in \citet[Ch.~II, \S\S2--3]{tyurin1978periods}.

title: Algebraic description of vector bundles on projective space
statement: For each \(n\geq0\), describe the finite-rank algebraic vector bundles on \(\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\) up to isomorphism. The precise requested form in the notes is a classification by proper graded exterior-algebra modules up to adding graded free summands. This problem belongs to the manuscript lecture of 13 February 1978; its corrected GP-1977 identifier records the actual academic year, while this package retains the requested catalogue record.
status: Solved in the stated representation-theoretic sense by \citet[Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}, received 10 January 1978 and published in the 1978 volume. Theorem~2 gives the derived categorical equivalence. No earlier problem ID in the supplied index states this exact projective-bundle problem; affine freeness (the Quillen--Suslin theorem) has different hypotheses.

title: Represent twisting by O(1) on the exterior-module side
statement: Given a proper graded exterior-algebra module \(V\), determine an operation whose associated bundle is \(\Phi(V)(1)\). The notes ask and answer this question within the same, miscatalogued 1978 lecture.
status: Solved: embed \(V\) into a finite graded free module, take the cokernel \(V^{\prime}\), and use \(W_j=V^{\prime}_{j+1}\). See \citet[remark~2 after Theorem~1]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}. The fibre long exact sequence independently checks the shift.
